July 2025}} is an American-Libyan professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Sagesse SC (basketball)|Sagesse Club]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]] (LBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Detroit Mercy Titans men's basketball|Detroit Mercy Titans]]. ==High school career== Bass attended [[Seaholm High School]] in [[Birmingham, Michigan]]. As a senior, he averaged 23.4 points and 12.4 rebounds per game. Bass earned Basketball Coaches Association of Michigan (BCAM) All-State Team and the Detroit News All-Metro North First Team honors. Regarded as a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Bass committed to play college basketball at [[Detroit Mercy Titans men's basketball|Detroit Mercy]].{{cite web |title=Phoenix Suns Sign Former Titan Standout Paris Bass |url=https://detroittitans.com/news/2021/12/31/mens-basketball-phoenix-suns-sign-former-titan-standout-paris-bass.aspx |website=[[Detroit Mercy Titans]] |access-date=January 1, 2022 |date=December 31, 2021}} ==College career== Bass [[redshirted]] his true freshman season. As a redshirt freshman, he averaged 12.4 points, 5.7 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game. Bass was named [[Horizon League]] Freshman of the Year. He missed the first eight games of his sophomore season with a suspension. Bass averaged 18.4 points, 8 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game as a sophomore, earning First-team All-Horizon League honors.On May 10, 2016, Bass was removed from the Detroit Mercy program.{{cite news |last=Farrell |first=Perry |title=Detroit Mercy leading scorer Paris Bass one of 2 removed from team |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2016/05/10/parris-bass-udm-basketball-detroit/84185336/ |access-date=January 1, 2022 |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=May 10, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Austria and NBA D-League (2016–2017)=== On July 27, 2016, Bass signed his first professional contract with the [[Traiskirchen Lions]] of the [[Austrian Basketball Bundesliga]].{{cite news |title=Former Titans Bass, Wilson to play basketball overseas |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2016/07/27/former-titans-bass-wilson-play-basketball-overseas/87642984/ |access-date=January 1, 2022 |work=[[The Detroit News]] |date=July 27, 2016}} He did not make his debut for Traiskirchen.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Paris-Bass/NBA/Phoenix-Suns/301948|title=Paris Bass|work=usbasket.com|access-date=January 4, 2022|url-access=subscription}} In February 2017, Bass signed with the [[Osceola Magic|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA D-League]].{{cite web |title=Former Titan Paris Bass Signs With NBDL's Erie BayHawks |url=https://detroittitans.com/news/2017/2/5/mens-basketball-former-titan-paris-bass-signs-with-nbdls-erie-bayhawks |website=[[Detroit Mercy Titans]] |access-date=January 1, 2022 |date=February 5, 2017}} In 15 games, he averaged 3.9 points and 2.7 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last=Windisch |first=Ti |title=Milwaukee Bucks Pre-Draft Workouts: Another Badger visits the Bucks |url=https://behindthebuckpass.com/2017/05/24/milwaukee-bucks-pre-draft-workouts-another-badger-visits-bucks/3/ |website=Behind the Bucks Pass |publisher=[[FanSided]] |access-date=January 1, 2022 |date=May 24, 2017}} ===Dominican, Taiwan, Puerto Rico, and Colombia (2018–2021)=== In 2018, Bass played for three teams in the Dominican Republic: El Million Yireh of the [[Torneo Superior de Baloncesto|TBS]], [[Titanes del Distrito Nacional|Titanes del Licey]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto|LNB]], and Jose Horacio Rodriguez of the Superior Basketball Tournament of Espaillat (BSE).{{cite web|url=https://elnuevodiario.com.do/en-gran-faena-paris-bass-anota-57-puntos-y-jose-horacio-domina-semifinal-del-bse/|title=En gran faena París Bass anota 57 puntos y José Horacio domina semifinal del BSE|work=elnuevodiario.com.do|date=October 4, 2018|access-date=January 4, 2022|language=es}} Between November 17 and December 15, 2018, Bass played for [[Kaohsiung Jeoutai Technology|Kinmen Kaoliang Liquor]] of the Taiwanese [[Super Basketball League]].{{cite news |last=Pan |first=Jason |title=Kinmen Kaoliang hand Dacin Tigers their fourth straight loss since opener |url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/sport/archives/2018/11/26/2003704946 |access-date=January 1, 2022 |work=[[Taipei Times]] |date=November 26, 2018}} In 2019, Bass played for four teams in the Dominican Republic: CDP Domingo Paulino Santiago of the Santiago League, Club Rafael Barias of the TBS, Jose Horacio Rodriguez of the BSE,{{cite web|url=https://elnacional.com.do/paris-bass-y-branden-dawson-conducen-al-jose-horacio-inicio-semifinal-basket-de-moca/|title=París Bass y Branden Dawson conducen al José Horacio inicio semifinal basket de Moca|work=elnacional.com.do|date=August 4, 2019|access-date=January 4, 2022|language=es}} and [[Indios de San Francisco de Macorís]] of the LNB.{{cite web |last=Garcia |first=Hector |title=Paris Bass es cuarto refuerzo Indios de San Francisco |url=https://momentodeportivord.com/paris-bass-es-cuarto-refuerzo-indios-de-san-francisco/ |website=Momento Deportivo |access-date=January 1, 2022 |language=es |date=September 8, 2019}} With Indios de San Francisco, he helped the team win the championship and was named MVP of the tournament and of the Final Series.{{cite web|last=Gomez|first=Renso|url=https://elfildeo.com/nba/paris-bass-nba-suns-phoenix-lakers-rafael-baris-lnb-indios/260987/2021/|title=Paris Bass rumbo a la NBA con los Suns de Phoenix Suns|work=elfildeo.com|date=December 30, 2021|access-date=January 4, 2022|language=es}} In January 2020, Bass re-joined CDP Domingo Paulino Santiago of the Santiago League and averaged 23.5 points, 12.2 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.3 steals per game. Bass joined the [[Atléticos de San Germán]] of the Puerto Rican [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] on March 5, 2020.{{cite web |last=Modestti |first=Luis |title=Paris Bass (ex CDP) signs at San German |url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/news/622024/Paris-Bass-(ex-CDP)-signs-at-San-German |website=Latinbasket |access-date=January 1, 2022 |date=March 5, 2020}} In his first season with the team, he averaged 22.1 points and 10.6 rebounds per game. On September 24, 2020, Bass signed with Cimarrones del Choco of the [[Baloncesto Profesional Colombiano]].{{cite web |title=Cimarrones add Bass to their roster, ex San German |url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Colombia/news/645809/Former-players:-Cimarrones-add-Bass-to-their-roster,-ex-San-German |website=Latinbasket |access-date=January 1, 2022 |date=September 24, 2020}} In March 2021, Bass re-joined CDP Domingo Paulino Santiago for a third stint. He also had a second stint with Club Rafael Barias between May 5 and June 1, 2021. He re-joined the Atléticos de San Germán in July 2021 and averaged 22.7 points per game during the season.{{cite news |date=December 30, 2021 |title=Paris Bass, refuerzo de los Atléticos de San Germán, firmará contrato de 10 días con los Suns de Phoenix |language=es |work=[[El Nuevo Día]] |url=https://www.elnuevodia.com/deportes/baloncesto/notas/paris-bass-refuerzo-de-los-atleticos-de-san-german-firmara-contrato-de-10-dias-con-los-suns-de-phoenix/ |access-date=January 1, 2022}} ===South Bay Lakers / Phoenix Suns (2021–2022)=== In October 2021, Bass joined the [[South Bay Lakers]] of the [[NBA G League]] after a successful tryout.{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Kioski|title=South Bay Finalizes Training Camp Roster|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-finalizes-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=January 1, 2022}} He was named to the NBA G League All-Showcase Team.{{cite web |title=Paris Bass Earns NBA Call-Up with Phoenix Suns |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/paris-bass-earns-nba-call-up-with-phoenix-suns/n-5777661 |website=Our Sports Central |access-date=January 1, 2022 |date=December 31, 2021}} On December 31, 2021, Bass signed a 10-day contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]] via the hardship exemption.{{cite web |last=Olson |first=Kellan |title=Phoenix Suns sign F Paris Bass to 10-day hardship deal |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2951072/suns-sign-f-paris-bass-to-10-day-hardship-deal/ |website=Arizona Sports |access-date=January 1, 2022 |date=December 31, 2021}} He signed a second 10-day contract with the Suns on January 12.{{cite news |title=Suns' Paris Bass: Joining Suns again |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/suns-paris-bass-joining-suns-again/ |access-date=January 12, 2022 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 12, 2022}} On January 22, 2022, Bass was reacquired by the South Bay Lakers.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 22, 2022|access-date=January 22, 2022}} Bass joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster.{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612747/lakers |access-date=July 21, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} In his Lakers Summer League debut, Bass scored fifteen points, six rebounds, and three blocks in a 100–66 win against the [[Miami Heat]].{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers vs Miami Heat Jul 2, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/game/lal-vs-mia-1322200001/box-score#box-score |access-date=July 21, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} ===Salt Lake City Stars (2022–2023)=== On September 14, 2022, Bass signed with the [[Utah Jazz]],{{Cite web |last=Hundman |first=Gabby |date=September 14, 2022 |title=Utah Jazz Sign Paris Bass |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-paris-bass |access-date=September 16, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} but was waived 2 days later.{{Cite web |last=Hundman |first=Gabby |date=September 16, 2022 |title=Utah Jazz Waive Bass and Sneed |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-bass-and-sneed |access-date=September 16, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On October 23, 2022, Bass joined the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] training camp roster.{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/stars-announce-2022-23-training-camp-roster/n-5892964|title=Stars Announce 2022-23 Training Camp Roster|website=oursportscentral.com|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}} On January 1, 2023, he was waived.{{cite
